title: Annual Accounts
summary: The ECB's Annual Accounts for 2025 show a balance sheet of €603.3 billion, contracted by €37.3 billion from the prior year primarily due to ceased reinvestments under asset purchase programmes. The ECB recorded a loss of €1,254 million, significantly lower than 2024, driven by reduced interest expense from the net TARGET liability.
key_points: ECB balance sheet stood at €603.3 billion in 2025, a contraction of €37.3 billion year-over-year
Balance sheet decline was driven by the Eurosystem no longer reinvesting principal payments from maturing securities under asset purchase programmes
ECB recorded a loss of €1,254 million for 2025, down significantly from 2024
The loss reduction was primarily due to decreased interest expense from the net TARGET liability
Losses will remain on the balance sheet to be offset against future profits
The page also links to Annual Accounts for prior years (2024, 2023, 2022, 2021)
why_it_matters: This document provides the ECB's own financial position and is distinct from policy decisions. The balance sheet contraction reflects the passive impact of maturing APP securities not being reinvested—a technical/mechanical effect of the ECB's existing framework rather than an active policy shift. The TARGET-related loss reflects intra-Eurosystem imbalances but does not directly impact monetary policy transmission or market conditions.
macro_context: The source contains minimal macro context as it focuses on the ECB's own accounting rather than macroeconomic conditions or forward-looking policy signals. The balance sheet contraction (€37.3 billion) reflects passive wind-down mechanics, not an active tightening or easing stance.
market_structure_context: The cessation of APP reinvestments contributes to gradual balance sheet reduction. This affects the composition of Eurosystem assets but is a known, telegraphed mechanical process rather than a market structure event.
